texts.facts: Despite that peremptory direction, no counter affidavit has been filed. Consequently this matter proceeds ex parte. The petitioner who runs a retail business of selling fish, meat and poultry assails the orders passed by the respondent Nos. 2 and 3 cancelling his licence and sealing the premises from which the business was being conducted. The record reflects that the Licensing Authority inspected the premises and called upon the petitioner to explain the source from which poultry and meat was being obtained. Although he was granted 15 days' time to furnish the requisite explanation, no reply appears to have been submitted. In light of the failure on the part of the petitioner to explain the source from which the poultry items were being obtained, the Licensing Authority proceeded to Naim Ahmad vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 1 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57654335/ 1 cancel the permission accorded to the petitioner under the provisions of the Food Safety Standards Act 2006 by an order of 04 April 2018. Aggrieved by that order the petitioner approached the Additional Commissioner. That revision which was preferred has come to be dismissed by the order of 19 November 2018.
